'''Zehev Tadmor''' ({{langx|he|זאב תדמור}}; born 1937) is a retired Israeli [[chemical engineer]] who has served as distinguished professor, president, and chairman of the [[Technion-Israel Institute of Technology]]. He is also chairman of the Samuel Neaman Institute for Advanced Studies in Science and Technology, a policy research center. His main research interest is [[Polymer engineering|polymer]] and [[plastics engineering]] and processing. He won the [[Emet Prize]] in 2005.

==Biography==

Tadmor received his BSc and MSc degrees in [[chemical engineering]] from the [[Technion-Israel Institute of Technology]], and his doctorate in chemical engineering from the [[Stevens Institute of Technology]] in New Jersey.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|url=https://emetprize.com/|title=פרס א.מ.ת. &#124; פרס האמנות, המדע והתרבות|website=emetprize.com}}</ref>

Tadmor's main research interest is [[Polymer engineering|polymer]] and [[plastics engineering]] and processing.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.usistf.org/about/board-of-directors/zehev-tadmor/|title=Dr. Zehev Tadmor|date=March 14, 2014|publisher=US-Israel Science & Technology Foundation|access-date=January 27, 2020|archive-date=January 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200127062643/http://www.usistf.org/about/board-of-directors/zehev-tadmor/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="auto3"/> He has published three books and 75 papers in the field.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto3"/>

He worked for the [[Western Electric Company]] as a Senior Research Engineer, and then joined the Technion Faculty of Chemical Engineering in 1968.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|url=https://nae.edu/29852/Dr-Zehev-Tadmor|title=Dr. Zehev Tadmor|website= National Academy of Engineering}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.neaman.org.il/EN/Zehev-Tadmor|title=Distinguished Prof. (Emeritus) Zehev Tadmor|website=Samuel Neaman Institute for Advanced Studies in Science and Technology}}</ref> In 1975 Tadmor was appointed a Technion full professor, and in 1988 a Distinguished Technion Professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering.<ref name="auto2"/> From 1984 to 1988 he served as Dean of the Department of Chemical Engineering.<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto3"/><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/business/1.5106888|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624152711/https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/business/1.5106888|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 24, 2018|title=Mission for Israel 2028: Stay Ahead of the Game|first=Guy|last=Rolnik|date=January 12, 2011|work=Haaretz}}</ref>

Tadmor served as President of The Technion from 1990 to 1998.<ref name="auto3"/><ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto4"/><ref name="auto"/> He is Chairman of the Technion-Israel Institute of Technology.<ref name="auto4"/><ref name="auto"/>

He is also Chairman of the Samuel Neaman Institute for Advanced Studies in Science and Technology, a policy research center.<ref name="auto3"/><ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto1"/>

==Accolades==
Tadmor was elected a member of the US [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1991 for creative research and his influence on the practice of [[polymer]] processing.<ref name="auto4"/><ref name="auto3"/>  He is also an elected member of the [[Israel Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="auto3"/>

He was inducted into the Polymer Processing Hall of Fame in 1993, and received the [[Rotary International|Rotary Prize]] for "Outstanding Contributions to Higher Education in Israel".<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto3"/> Tadmor was awarded an Honorary Doctorate in Industrial Chemistry from the [[University of Bologna]] in 1995, and received the [[Society of Plastics Engineers]] of the USA "Extrusion Division Distinguished Service Award" and "Outstanding Achievement Award in Plastics Engineering and Technology".<ref name="auto2"/><ref name="auto3"/> He won the [[Emet Prize]] in 2005 in Exact Sciences in the field of chemical engineering "for his original and pioneering contribution to the field of polymer processing, transforming it into a new and important engineering discipline, and for his academic leadership as a pre-eminent mentor and researcher in chemical engineering in Israel."<ref name="auto3"/>
